text: A stack of L phase-only diffractive layers with no optical nonlinearity between them is mathematically what, and where does its only nonlinearity come from?
choices: A genuinely deep nonlinear network, because each phase layer is nonlinear
A quadratic network, because the phase is squared at every layer
A single complex-linear operator M; the only nonlinearity is the |.|^2 intensity measurement at the output detector
A random projection followed by a trained optical softmax
explanation: Phase-only layers are linear, so L of them compose to one complex-linear map M = H_d*diag(t^L)...diag(t^1); no nonlinearity acts until the detector applies |.|^2 at the output. This is why a D2NN needs no optical nonlinearity to classify (the magnitude-squared supplies the decision surface) yet has bounded capacity. Phase multiplication is linear, and there is no optical softmax.
